sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a single tooth measuring 0.25 mm in height and 0.26 mm in width.
This tooth features a gracile crown morphology distinct from other known Jurassic batomorphs, suggesting a consistent referral to the superfamily Batoidea, which includes skates and rays.
The fossil was recovered from the Grimmen Clay Pit within the Wolgast Formation.
The fossil tooth is considered allochthonous due to extensive post-mortem breakage likely caused by reworking.
Researchers suggest Antiquaobatis used less specialized, opportunistic feeding strategies based on its tooth morphology.
Antiquaobatis belongs to the parent group Rajiformes and is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Antiquaobatis lived in Europe during the Early Jurassic, specifically the Pliensbachian, from 192.9 to 184.2 million years ago.
It is debated whether the fossil originated locally or was moved from the Polish Basin, where sea flooding is evidenced by ammonite finds.
